idiom_name: session struct owning HashMap<Id, Rc<RefCell<Entity>>> / Arc<RwLock<Entity>>
implementation_notes: Rust database libraries (Diesel, sqlx) materialise owned values per query and provide no session identity map, so the classic structure is hand-written: a session/repository struct owns a HashMap<Id, _> and hands out the stored handle on a hit, inserting on a miss. Rust forces the sharing decision into the type: Rc<RefCell<T>> for a single-threaded session, Arc<RwLock<T>> when the session crosses threads (async tasks), or Weak when the map must not own. The classic form is justified only when object identity itself carries meaning; otherwise passing ids and values is more idiomatic than sharing instances.
pitfalls: Rc/RefCell is single-threaded only: sharing a session across tasks needs Arc<RwLock>, and mixing them is a compile error at best, a deadlock at worst.
RefCell borrow panics when an entity is borrowed while a mutation or iteration is live - keep borrows short and never hold one across a call.
Strong maps keep every entity alive for the whole session; use Weak when the map is only an index, and clear it at the unit-of-work boundary.
